components.title: The Water Cycle
components.subtitle: How water moves through land, sea, and sky

components.text: Heat from the sun warms liquid water in oceans, lakes, and rivers. As it warms, molecules gain enough energy to escape into the air as water vapour, an invisible gas.
Water vapour rises and cools. When it cools enough, it changes back into tiny liquid droplets that gather around dust particles, forming clouds.
When cloud droplets grow heavy, they fall as rain, snow, sleet, or hail. Some water soaks into the ground, some runs off into rivers, and the cycle begins again.

components.title: Worked example: a puddle disappears
components.body: A puddle forms after a morning rain. By noon, sunlight has warmed it, so water evaporates into the air. The vapour cools higher up, condenses into a small cloud, and may later fall again as rain.
components.takeaway: The same water can move through every stage of the cycle.

questions.question: What process turns liquid water into water vapour?
questions.explanation: Evaporation happens when the sun's heat gives water molecules enough energy to escape as vapour.

questions.question: Which stage forms clouds?
questions.explanation: Condensation occurs when water vapour cools and turns into tiny droplets that form clouds.

questions.question: Rain, snow, sleet, and hail are all forms of what?
questions.explanation: Precipitation is any water that falls from clouds to the ground.
